case_number: Criminal Appeal No.97 of 2022 with Criminal Appeal No.98 of 2022

parties.respondent: The State of Uttar Pradesh & Anr.

summary: The appellant, father of the deceased, challenged the Allahabad High Court's bail order granting bail to accused persons in a serious criminal case involving offences under Sections 302, 307, 147, 148, 149, 323, 504, 506, and 34 IPC. The Supreme Court noted that the High Court relied on incorrect facts—such as accused not being named in the FIR and delayed recording of witness statements—both factually inaccurate and not even the accused’s case. The Court observed that the High Court failed to consider the gravity of the offence, the role of the accused in a common unlawful assembly under Section 149 IPC, and did not apply proper bail considerations. The bail order was deemed mechanical and lacking reasoned analysis.
legal_provisions_cited: Anil Kumar Yadav Vs. State (NCT of Delhi) (2018) 12 SCC 129
final_judgment: The appeals were allowed, the impugned bail orders set aside, and the respondents No.2 were directed to surrender to custody forthwith.
